pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered in full — custom programme, weekly check-ins with the reasoning explained, video form correction, plus a five to ten minute morning mobility routine aimed at his knees. Response was 'that sounds pretty straightforward' and no questions. When asked what stood out he gave the reason he came: 'Just that it takes everything into account, rather than, like, lifting, you're just working on your muscles. So like, I need better posture, like better everything.'

The only pillar he volunteered a positive reaction to: 'Nothing, really. I'm just more excited to find out about the intermittent fasting and see what windows I could eat and stuff like that, you know?' The pitch had been tailored to his actual constraint — a shared kitchen, cooking fatigue and a protein baseline that survives the nights he cannot be bothered — which is why it landed.

He had already named it as the thing he needed before the pillar was presented — 'I just need the extra structure. I need the extra push. Cause I plateau without it' — and confirmed it when asked what stood out overall: 'I definitely just could use the accountable part.' He then endorsed the rep's diagnosis of why his last programme failed at six weeks of eight.

anchors.raw: I paid for Anatoly's program and it was like a couple hundred... I was in really good shape. I'm not gonna lie. I made it through, I think, six weeks of it... yeah, I was in really good shape. It worked, it worked well.
anchors.competitor: Anatoly — an eight-week video programme with routines, meals and videos
anchors.note: The most damaging anchor in the batch. A roughly thirty-fold price gap against a product this specific prospect bought, used and got results from. The rep's counter was correct — it was a video course with no coaching, and he abandoned it at six weeks of eight for exactly the reason coaching exists — but a correct diagnosis has nowhere to land when the only product is $6,000.

anchors.raw: it's definitely not something I could afford, even like on monthly, because that's like $1,000 a month.
anchors.note: He converted the total to a monthly figure the instant it was quoted and rejected both forms at once, which closed off the instalment route before it could be offered. Every prospect in this batch did the same arithmetic within seconds of hearing $6,000.

anchors.raw: I just got too much going on right now with moving, and I got a lot of bills I can't even afford to think about adding another bill
anchors.note: Moving costs after a breakup plus existing bills he describes as already unaffordable. Sizeable and immediate, and disclosed only after the price — a budget question at the top of the call would have surfaced it in thirty seconds.

anchors.raw: I just found him literally like a week or two ago.
anchors.note: One to two weeks of following Trevor, versus six months for Saagar Patel-Francis and a long-standing following for Ken Dunham, the two prospects who were ready to buy. Low familiarity means the price has no reputational scaffolding to rest on, and it is a cheap thing to check at the top of a call.

unmet_demand.want: Structured kettlebell programming with real accountability at a price under $6,000
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There are two tiers, $6,000 and $9,000, and nothing below. He has already proven he will pay for programming and that a programme without accountability fails for him at around six weeks. That is a precisely described customer for a mid-tier product that does not exist.

unmet_demand.want: A way to build kettlebell workouts himself
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This is what he left to do: 'I'll probably just explore it on my own, like, try to find out a way to build out kettlebell workouts.' There is no self-serve programme, template or paid course to sell him, so a prospect who confirmed the value three times and committed to going all in walked out with nothing and will assemble it from free content.

unmet_demand.want: Athletic carryover to flag football next summer
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He named it twice as a driver — 'when I play football next summer, I want to be in way better shape than this' — and the rep referenced athleticism once in passing during the presentation. No sport-specific framing, no seasonal timeline, and it was never used to create urgency despite being a dated goal.
